## The floor detector and the redo decision {#sec-ch08-redo}

### Summary

Everything else in this chapter keeps the state admissible or records that it could not. This is the
mechanism that decides the step was bad enough to take again, and it is the closest thing snapy has to a
positivity failure path.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Decide whether the step just taken must be redone: a floor test on the primitives plus the limiter marks.

**Data.** In: `hydro_u`, the floors, the `EfStatus` marks and latches, the implicit clamp. Out: a cause bit set.

**Placement.** In `check_redo`, after the stages of a step and before the clock advances (@sec-ch01-driver).

**Activation.** Always; a hit is a primitive at or below $1.001$ times a floor, a NaN, a mark, a latch or the clamp.

**Guarantee / limits.** Detection only: a redo repeats the step and the redo budget of @sec-ch09 ends the loop.

**Evidence.** `[C7]` of `floors_check`; the redo cases of `test_forcing.<b>`.
:::

### Derivation

The test is a margin above the floor rather than equality with it, in `local_redo_flag_tensor`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). A minimum interior density at or
below $1.001$ times the density floor counts as a hit. The same holds for pressure where there is a pressure row.
Testing equality with the floor would miss a cell that was floored and then nudged by a later operation; the margin
catches the neighbourhood of the floor instead. `[C7]` nudges a just-floored cell by fifteen relative amounts from
$10^{-16}$ up to $10^{-3}$. The margin counts all fifteen as hits. Equality counts only two, the unnudged cell and
the single nudge below machine epsilon, so thirteen are hits the margin keeps and equality loses. A density $1.002$
times the floor is a hit under neither. `[C4]` covers the marking itself, including that it happens only from the
interior [check `src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.out`].

Two orderings around it matter, and the code states both. In the decision the floor test runs first: it converts
the state to primitives to test them, and that conversion may itself make a limiter repair and set a mark. The marks
are read after the floor test, so that such a repair counts in this decision (`limiter_marks`, read in
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). The marks are reset only later, in
`apply_redo`, once a redo has been decided and the state restored: the conversions of the floor test and of the
restore must not mark the step that is redone (`reset_limiter_marks`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

### Numerical method

The detector does not read the state back to the host. `local_redo_flag_tensor` builds one small device tensor per
block, in this order ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}):

1. `floor`: the margin test on the interior primitives, density and, where there is one, pressure;
2. `clamp`: whether the implicit dry clamp of @sec-ch08-vic acted in the step, read from `dry_clamp_step`
   ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitHydroImpl::dry_clamp_step >}});
3. and 4. the two limiter marks of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter, `limiter_marks` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.hpp
   EquationOfStateImpl::limiter_marks >}}): a floor patched an interior cell, and an interior NaN;
5. the saturation adjustment's unconverged cells, row 0 of kintera's failure counter (@sec-ch08-satadj);
6. the implicit solve's failure latch (@sec-ch06);
7. the step's deferred vapour-repair failures (@sec-ch08-fixvapor);
8. the ideal-moist heat-capacity latch.

The marks, the vapour failures and the heat-capacity latch are slots of the block's `EfStatus` (@sec-ch08-efstatus).
`read_redo_flags` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::read_redo_flags >}}) makes the one
device-to-host copy and folds entries 7 and 8 into the limiter cause. `decide_retry`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::decide_retry >}}) takes the maximum over the local blocks and,
with a process group, over the ranks, so a hit in any block redoes every block. `apply_redo`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}) prints the causes by name (`floor`, `clamp`,
`limiter`, `nan`, `saturation`, `vic-solve`), rolls the flux register back, restores the state and resets the
marks.

**Why a margin, and why the marks are reset.** Three facts of the code.

1. The test is `(min > 1.001 * floor).logical_not()`, a margin above the floor rather than equality
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). So a floored cell nudged by a
   later operation is still a hit. `[C7]` counts 15 of 15 nudges up to $10^{-3}$ relative, against 2 for equality.
2. The comparison is negated, so a NaN, which fails every comparison, counts as a hit.
3. The marks are read after the floor test, whose conversion may mark a repair that then counts in this decision
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). They are reset in `apply_redo`
   after the redo is decided and the state restored, so the floor test's and the restore's conversions do not mark
   the redone step ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

: Code map of the floor detector. {#tbl-ch08-redo-code}

**How to use it.** Nothing is set; the detector reads the floors of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter. The floor test is
these lines ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}):

```cpp
  // negated so a NaN, which fails every comparison, counts as a hit
  auto floor = (w[IDN].min() > 1.001 * eos->density_floor()).logical_not();
  if (w.size(0) > IPR) {  // shallow water carries no pressure row
    floor = floor.logical_or(
        (w[IPR].min() > 1.001 * eos->pressure_floor()).logical_not());
  }
```

`w` is the primitive state restored from `hydro_u` on the interior, and `eos` the equation-of-state options. A
driver sees the result as the positive return of `check_redo` and repeats the cycle (@sec-ch01-driver).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A redo repeats the step; it does not make the step succeed. A column that floors at every step size
  will keep flooring, and the redo budget of the time-integration chapter is what ends the loop.
:::

1. **The margin is a constant.** The factor $1.001$ is not derived and not configurable. A cell
   legitimately sitting a tenth of a per cent above the floor is read as a hit.
2. **Detection is per block.** One floored cell marks the whole block for a redo, and nothing records
   which cell it was.
